title: What does the hub show first when you open it on your phone?
context: On a phone the hub opens on the thread list, so answering anything takes a tap into Needs you first, and moving between threads means going back to the list each time. Decision 12 set the desktop layout; the phone layout was never decided. Found in the ux-review round.

options.name: Needs you first, list behind Back
options.summary: Open straight into Needs you when something waits (thread list when nothing does). Back still shows the list. Nothing else changes.
pros: One tap less for the common case
cons: Moving between agents still goes through the list

options.name: Bottom bar with four places
options.summary: A bar at the bottom with Needs you, Orchestrator, Agents and Map, each with its count. Opens on Needs you when something waits. The map strip stays on top as decided.
pros: Every place one thumb tap away
Feels like a phone app from the home screen
cons: A second way to navigate next to the strip

options.name: Leave the list first
options.summary: Keep today's behaviour; notification taps already land on the card.
cons: Opening the app yourself always costs an extra tap

recommendation: Most phone visits are to answer something; landing on Needs you fixes that at almost no cost. B is worth it only if you move between agents a lot on the phone.
